parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/application forms one cohesive application-service layer. It has six use-case classes that share one pattern: inject domain ports, call domain behaviour, persist, and map the result to a DTO. One shared file, dtos.ts, holds the boundary types and the mappers. Each use case returns its result through toOrderDto or toStockLevelDto, so none bypasses the module's own mapping abstraction. Business invariants live in the domain, not here: state transitions go through Order.cancel() and Order.moveTo(), and stock rules go through StockReservationService.reserve() and release(). They are not repeated across use cases. One thing does repeat: CancelOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase and TransitionOrderUseCase each contain the same 'findById or throw NotFoundError' guard. That is a small lookup idiom, not a business rule or invariant, so it does not fail the rubric. It could still be pulled into a shared helper. ListStockLevelsUseCase covers stock rather than orders, but it is the same order/inventory application concern and follows the same pattern, so it does not split the module.
